item.title: Indonesia Aims for $17.5 Billion Transactions in Trade Expo
item.description: Jakarta. The government-run Trade Expo Indonesia is seeking to amass at least $17.5 billion in transactions, exceeding last year’s previous target. Every year, the Trade Ministry hosts an annual international exhibition in a bid to spur the country’s export performance. The government is also betting on this expo to link small businesses with global markets. “In 2025, we were aiming for $16.5 billion, but we managed to record $22.8 billion in transactions. item.title: Danantara Enters Year Two With $2.7 Trillion Ambition and Rising Scrutiny
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund Danantara marked its first anniversary on Feb. 24 with an ambitious mandate: oversee the country’s vast state-owned enterprise (SOE) portfolio and steer multibillion-dollar strategic projects. President Prabowo Subianto has consistently positioned Danantara as a cornerstone of his economic agenda. Speaking to American business leaders in Washington last week, he said all state-owned assets had been consolidated under Danantara to accelerate investment.

item.title: Rural Cooperative Drive Sparks Auto Import Dispute and Retail Tensions
item.description: Jakarta. The rapid formation of tens of thousands of rural cooperatives is creating ripple effects far beyond the countryside, unsettling Indonesia’s automotive industry and reigniting debate over modern retail expansion. The government aims to establish 80,000 “Merah Putih” village cooperatives, with thousands inaugurated simultaneously and 30,000 expected to be operational by the end of May. item.title: Beyond Tariffs: Indonesia’s Uneven Pact with Washington
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia’s Agreement on Reciprocal Tariff (ART) with the United States is increasingly seen by economists as a structural policy gamble rather than a straightforward export breakthrough. The deal removes US tariffs on 1,819 Indonesian products. item.title: Russia Respects Indonesia’s Gaza Peace Board Status, But Stays Skeptical
item.description: Jakarta. A Russian diplomat has said that Moscow “respects” Indonesia’s membership in the Board of Peace for Gaza, but remains skeptical of whether this group can be the cure for conflict if it does not involve Palestinians. item.title: JCI Falls 1.35% at Open as S&P Warning and US Solar Tariffs Weigh
item.description: Jakarta. Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) opened sharply lower on Friday, sliding 111 points or 1.35% to 8,211, as investors reacted to fresh US trade measures and mounting fiscal concerns. The benchmark moved within a range of 8,152–8,214 in early trade. Volume reached 4.94 billion shares with turnover of Rp 1.7 trillion ($101.32 million) across more than 249,000 transactions. item.title: Prabowo Ends Global Diplomacy Tour with Fresh UAE Investment Pledge
item.description: Jakarta. President Prabowo Subianto concluded his weeks-long overseas tour in Abu Dhabi, where United Arab Emirates leader Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, widely known as MBZ, pledged to step up investment in Indonesia. Prabowo returned to Jakarta on Friday morning after departing on Feb. 16 for Washington. item.title: Antam Gold Extends Rally as Global Market Sees Profit-Taking
item.description: Jakarta. Gold prices extended gains for a second straight day on Friday as Antam bullion climbed Rp 6,000 to Rp 3,045,000 ($181.57) per gram, approaching its record high despite global profit-taking in precious metals markets. Data from the Logam Mulia website shows the increase follows Thursday’s Rp 16,000 jump, which pushed Antam gold to Rp 3,039,000 per gram. item.title: Not a Shutdown: Govt Plans to Curb New Minimarkets in Rural Areas
item.description: Jakarta. item.title: End of An Era: Modern Retail Leaves Indonesia with Just 3.9 Million Warung
item.description: Jakarta. Rapid expansion of modern retailers have led to a sharp decline in Indonesia's mom-and-pop stores, coloquially known as "warung kelontong", according to the street vendor association APKLI.
